subject: science
passage: Wind, ice, and rivers constantly wear rock away from the Himalayas, carrying huge amounts of sediment down to the plains of South Asia. One might expect this steady erosion to make the mountains slowly shrink. ______ much of the range is still rising, because the Indian tectonic plate continues to push northward into Asia, forcing rock upward faster, in many places, than erosion can remove it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence sets up an expectation: erosion should make the mountains shrink. The last sentence says the opposite is true: much of the range is still rising. A transition that signals a contrast with the expectation is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Erosion would not cause the mountains to rise; the rise happens despite erosion. The "because" later in the sentence may make a cause word tempting.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Rising mountains are not an example of the shrinking that one might expect; they go against it.
explanation.C: Correct. "However" signals that the mountains are rising, contrary to the expectation that erosion would make them shrink.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals agreement, but rising contradicts the expected shrinking.
